confidence.rationale: The concerns are present at the current upstream head and are backed by unresolved upstream Copilot threads plus a fresh fork Copilot review. The elevated trust pattern conflicts with the locked-handle guidance in src/common/updating/installer.h and installer.cpp.

proposed_comments.body:
Please address the unresolved cleanup-tool blockers before this merges. The script runs elevated while consuming per-user MSI and bundle registration data, so the validation needs to be bound to the exact package/executable that will be removed or launched.

The current code still trusts Windows Installer registration metadata (`ProductName`, `Publisher`, and `LocalPackage`) instead of validating the cached MSI database itself against the known PowerToys UpgradeCode/ProductCode, and it validates bundle executable paths before later reopening those paths with `Start-Process`. That leaves a path-swap window for user-writable per-user bundle/cache paths. Please stage to an administrator-controlled location or otherwise hold a locked, verified handle through execution, matching the updater's TOCTOU guidance.

There is also a functional issue for standard users: requiring the whole script to run elevated changes HKCU, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, and the per-user MSI context to the administrator account, so it cannot clean the affected standard user's per-user install. Split the current-user cleanup from the elevated per-machine work, or explicitly preserve and operate on the originating user's SID/profile context. Finally, wait for captured PowerToys processes to exit with a bounded timeout instead of relying on `Stop-Process` plus a fixed one-second sleep before starting uninstall work.
